passages.title: Save the Sharks!
passages.body: Sharks are in danger. Every year, millions of sharks are killed for their fins. This is very cruel. Fishermen catch the sharks, cut off their fins, and throw the sharks back into the sea. Without their fins, the sharks cannot swim, and they soon die. Sharks are at the top of the food chain. They help keep the ocean's ecosystem healthy. If all the sharks disappear, the whole ocean will be in danger. Some people eat shark fins because they think they are good for health. But no scientific studies have shown this. We should all help save the sharks. We can refuse to eat shark fins and ask others to do the same.

passages.title: Rethink, Reuse, Recycle
passages.body: We all create waste every day. But there are three simple ways to help the earth: rethink, reuse, and recycle. First, rethink. Before you buy something, ask if you really need it. The more we buy, the more waste we make. Second, reuse. Many things can be used again. You can use a glass bottle to hold water, or turn an old box into a useful container. Third, recycle. Paper, glass, and metal can all be recycled. They can be made into new things. If we all take action, we can make a big difference. Saving the earth is not hard. It just takes a little thought and effort from everyone.

passages.title: The Bottle House
passages.body: In a small town, there was a man named Mr. Lee. He loved to reuse old things. One day, he had an idea. He decided to build a house using old glass bottles. People thought he was crazy. "You can't build a house from rubbish!" they said. But Mr. Lee did not give up. He collected thousands of bottles that people had thrown away. He put them to good use. After two years, the house was finished. It was beautiful and colorful. The sun shone through the bottles like a rainbow. Now, people come from far away to see the bottle house. Mr. Lee showed everyone that old things can become a work of art.

passages.title: Plastic or Paper?
passages.body: When we go shopping, we often have to choose between plastic bags and paper bags. Which is better for the earth? Plastic bags are cheap and strong. But they are very harmful to the environment. They do not break down for hundreds of years. Many plastic bags end up in the sea, where they hurt animals. Paper bags break down more easily, but making them uses many trees. So what is the best choice? The answer is simple: use a reusable bag! A reusable bag can be used many times. It saves money and helps the earth. Next time you go shopping, remember to bring your own bag.

passages.title: Small Actions, Big Difference
passages.body: Saving the earth is not only the job of governments. Each of us can help, too. There are many small actions we can take. We can turn off the lights when we leave a room. This saves energy. We can ride bikes or take public transportation instead of driving cars. This makes the air cleaner. We can use less paper and recycle what we use. This saves trees. We can carry a reusable water bottle instead of buying plastic ones. We can also tell our friends and family to do the same. These small actions may seem unimportant, but together they can make a big difference. The earth is our home, and we must take care of it.

passages.title: Green School Notice
passages.body: GREEN SCHOOL WEEK! Let's work together to protect our environment. Here is how you can help. MONDAY: Turn off lights and computers when you leave the classroom. Save energy! TUESDAY: Bring a reusable water bottle. Do not use plastic ones. WEDNESDAY: Use both sides of your paper. Save trees! THURSDAY: Put rubbish in the right bins. We will recycle paper, glass, and metal. FRIDAY: Walk or ride a bike to school if you can. Remember, the earth is our home. Every small action counts. Let's take action together and make our school a greener place. Thank you for your help!
